title: Ex-General Gadi Eisenkot Tapped to Form Israeli Government as Netanyahu Battles for Political Survival
snippet: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has invited former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to assemble a governing coalition after last month's election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu short of a majority.
content:
JERUSALEM — Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked former army chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming the nation's next government following a bitterly contested and deadlocked election, delivering a major setback to incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bid to retain power.

Netanyahu’s religious-nationalist bloc lost its parliamentary majority in the Oct. 27 vote. Although his Likud party remains the largest single faction in the 120-seat Knesset with 27 seats, his broader coalition secured only 53 seats — well short of the 61 needed to govern.

Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar party, secured the initial mandate after receiving nominations from an alliance of center-left, right-wing, and Arab-led parties eager to end Netanyahu's record run as prime minister. Israel's Arab parties, which won an unprecedented 19 seats, backed Eisenkot to block Netanyahu despite the former general's refusal to include them directly in his government.

A Narrow Path to a Majority Coalition

Eisenkot now has 28 days, with the possibility of a two-week extension, to negotiate a functioning governing coalition. In a statement posted to X shortly after the announcement, Eisenkot called for national consensus, writing, "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything I can to ensure we are worthy."

Political analysts warn, however, that Eisenkot faces a steep uphill battle. His primary options include forming a minority government supported on key votes by Arab lawmakers, forging a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties he previously shunned, or negotiating a national unity government with Netanyahu — an option Eisenkot has repeatedly sworn off.

If Eisenkot fails to secure 61 seats within the allotted timeframe, President Herzog can pass the mandate to another lawmaker. Should the parliamentary stalemate persist past a 100-day window, Israelis would be forced back to the polls for another general election.

A Military Veteran with Deep Personal Ties to the Conflict

The 66-year-old Eisenkot, a son of Moroccan immigrants, would become Israel's first prime minister of Mizrahi descent if successful. A relative newcomer to political life who entered parliament in 2022, Eisenkot briefly served in Netanyahu's emergency war cabinet following the Oct. 7, 2023, attack by Hamas before resigning to return to the opposition.

Eisenkot's public standing is heavily shaped by both his high-profile security background and personal sacrifice; his son and two nephews were killed fighting in Gaza. As a former military chief of staff, he is known for formulating the "Dahiyeh doctrine" during the 2006 war against Hezbollah in Lebanon, which calls for disproportionate force against host infrastructure during asymmetric conflict.

Despite his defense credentials, Eisenkot has drawn sharp contrasts with Netanyahu's far-right partners, including Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. Eisenkot has publicly criticized surging settler violence against Palestinians in the West Bank and criticized Netanyahu's management of the Gaza war, promising to restore strain on Israel's critical alliances with Western nations.
